subject: Marketplace vs Direct Contract — procurement questions and next steps
messages:

Subject: Redwood listing — marketplace vs direct contract (procurement questions)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Acme is reviewing options and has a couple of clarifying questions before we proceed:

1) Billing & PO: If we purchase via AWS Marketplace private offer vs a direct Redwood contract, how will invoicing and PO handling differ? Can we still get Net30 with a PO?

2) Pricing & discounts: Are the commercial terms identical when you sell through marketplace private offers (AWS/Azure/GCP)? Any channel fees/commissions that reduce the net price to Redwood, and does that change what we pay?

3) Support & SLAs: Will the SLA, credits, and support path be the same if buying through marketplace vs a direct contract? Who do we open severity-1 tickets with?

4) Data residency & entitlements: We need to ensure contractual language around data handling and the ability to add KMS keys in our account if we go private offer. Any differences?

5) Contract term and termination: Are early-termination/refund policies identical?

If you can reply with a short bulleted comparison and any links/docs, that would be great — we are trying to decide if the team should approve a marketplace purchase for speed, or if we need to route to legal for a direct contract.

Cheers,
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager
Acme Industries

Subject: Re: Redwood listing — marketplace vs direct contract (procurement questions)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short comparison and attached a PDF that highlights the practical differences and recommended path based on most buyer priorities. High-level summary below:

- Billing & PO:
  - Marketplace private offer: Marketplace issues the invoice; you accept a private offer and the marketplace processes billing. PO flows are usually supported but are enforced by marketplace billing cycles — many customers still get Net30 via marketplace private offer but final terms depend on marketplace (AWS/AWS Marketplace typically supports PO/Net30 for transactable private offers).
  - Direct contract: Redwood invoices directly; PO/Net30 is standard and handled directly with our finance team.

- Pricing & discounts:
  - Marketplace: There can be channel fees (marketplace commission) behind the scenes, but Redwood typically absorbs standard marketplace fees for small deals or passes an equivalent commercial offer via private offer. For larger committed deals we recommend a direct contract to ensure the exact committed discount and rebates are documented.

- Support & SLAs:
  - Marketplace purchase does not change support model — Redwood remains the support owner for product issues. SLA credits and escalation paths remain the same; for critical incidents you contact Redwood Support (support@redwood.com) and we'll escalate.

- Data residency & entitlements:
  - Private offers can be configured to run in your cloud account with customer-owned KMS keys when using our Private Deployment or Dedicated options. For hosted Marketplace SaaS offers that route through Redwood, we document entitlements in the private offer. Direct contract gives more flexibility and explicit contractual CTAs for data handling.

- Termination & refunds:
  - Marketplace policies sometimes limit refunds/processes compared to direct contracts. For multi-year committed pricing and custom termination terms, direct contract is safer.

Recommendation: If Acme wants speed and simpler procurement routing today, a marketplace private offer (AWS/Azure/GCP) is a good path. For committed discounts, custom data residency clauses, or extended support/enterprise SLAs, go direct. I attached a one-page comparison and our standard SaaS terms for reference.

Next steps:
- If you want a marketplace private offer, we can create an AWS Private Offer (I included the AWS offer link below) and our finance team will work with your PO/payment terms.
- If Acme prefers direct, I can loop in our legal (Evelyn Hart) to share a tracked redline.

Attachments: 2026-03-09_redwood_marketplace_vs_direct_comparison.pdf; redwood_standard_saas_terms_v2.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi all — quick note from legal on the common procurement questions:

- Marketplace private offer: We can accept private offer flows and work with the marketplace invoicing. If Acme requires specific indemnities, liability caps, or additional security language, those are easier to negotiate in a direct contract.

- PO/Net30: We routinely accept Net30 tied to a PO for marketplace private offers; please confirm the PO number and billing contact when you accept the offer.

- KMS & data residency: For our Private/ Dedicated deployments where customer manages cloud resources, we can add explicit KMS language. For hosted marketplace SaaS, we will document where logs/metadata are stored. If Acme needs contractually-binding residency guarantees, direct contract is preferable.

Let me know if you want a redline — I can prepare a lean direct contract that mirrors the marketplace commercial terms but adds the clauses Acme needs.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Samantha. To confirm and next steps: 

- PO timing: You can accept the AWS private offer first and then submit a PO for Redwood invoicing; workflows vary by buyer but we've completed this flow multiple times. If you prefer the PO in advance, we can pause creation until you provide it.
- Signature: Acceptance of the private offer in AWS Marketplace plus your order acceptance is typically sufficient; marketplace issues invoices to Acme. Redwood will still own the support and SLA commitments.
- Refunds/early termination: For a one-year pilot, the private offer will include the standard marketplace refund/termination process. If you want explicit carveouts (e.g., prorated refunds for material SLA breaches), we should do a short direct contract instead.

I'll open a ticket with our finance team to prepare the AWS Private Offer (offer id included below). If you want to proceed with the private offer, please confirm the pilot term and whether you'll provide a PO before acceptance.
